title: function-tool identity service and deprecation mitigation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Reducing customer-facing breakage when model tool schemas and legacy 'function' signatures diverge across OpenAI-style 'tools' and Redwood legacy functions. We need a lightweight identity service that canonicalizes tool/function names, tracks deprecation aliases, and exposes a stable routing API for the runtime and API gateway. Goal: provide deterministic name resolution, telemetry-friendly provenance, and an automated deprecation mitigation flow (aliases, warning headers, and gradual rerouting).
technical_design: 1) Identity registry: small service (k/v backed by Cockroach) that stores canonical_id, aliases, first_seen, schema_hash, compatibility_tier. 2) Resolution API: Resolve(name, context) -> canonical_id + confidence + migration_hint. 3) Runtime integration: inference runtime queries resolver with caching + TTL and falls back to fuzzy-heuristic algorithm if resolver returns low confidence. 4) Backcompat layer: API gateway inserts X-Tool-Alias headers and can optionally translate legacy payload fields per mapping table. 5) Migration tooling: CLI to upload alias mappings, perform batch audits of active toolcalls, and emit suggestion PRs to customer configs. Implementation notes: lightweight service in Go, gRPC + HTTP proxy, incremental rollout via feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: Resolver API returns canonical_id for 99% of calls in test corpus (95% confidence or higher)
Runtime obtains resolution with median latency < 3ms under normal load when cached
Gateway can attach alias provenance header and fall back to legacy-params translation for configured mappings
Automated audit found and flagged >90% of name collisions in sampled customer tooling from last 30 days
End-to-end e2e test that simulates OpenAI-style tool name and legacy function name divergence and verifies no behavioral regression
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy resolver behind feature flag to internal staging, route 5% of traffic, collect mismatch telemetry. Phase 2 (early customers): enable for customers who opt in to 'compatibility assistance' and run mapping audit. Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 50% then 100% while enabling auto-alias creation rules only after manual approvals. Phase 4: deprecation enforcement mode where high-confidence aliases are silently translated and low-confidence ones return a structured warning in-stream.

risks: Risk of false-positive aliasing leading to silent misrouting. Mitigations: confidence thresholds, manual approval for auto-creating aliases, and clear telemetry that surfaces changed call counts. Operational risk: resolver availability must be highly-available and cached aggressively to avoid added tail latency.
qa_steps: 1) Run audit tool against tenant corpus and verify suggested aliases. 2) Deploy resolver to staging and run synthetic traffic with known alias pairs. 3) Enable gateway translation mappings and validate headers and translated payloads. 4) Smoke test streaming and toolcalling end-to-end to ensure no change in token stream ordering.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates identity resolution from signature transformation. A follow-up ticket will own full parameter marshalling for legacy->tool payload conversions. Coordinate with runtime and console teams for rollout messaging. Consider exposing a 'compatibility score' in Console routing debug view.
